frequency_question: How often does the central bank successfully issue temporary liquidity instrument circulars within a sub-quarter timeline upon identifying liquidity overhang?
membership_rule: Includes all official RBI circulars introducing new standing or ad-hoc liquidity absorption mechanisms (such as incremental CRR or special deposit facilities); excludes routine repo/reverse repo rate adjustments.
provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 2 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 2 named instances of iCRR specifically; both executed well within the 96-day limit once initiated.
known_gaps: Limited strictly to iCRR nomenclature, though broader liquidity absorption tools follow identical administrative paths.
skeleton: RBI monetary policy operational adjustments via circulars divided by total economic management periods requiring liquidity tightening
multiplier: 2 observed distinct iCRR-type deployment episodes in past liquidity overhang cycles over 15 years, where each took under 10 business days from conceptualization to formal notification.
validity_reason: Central bank internal regulatory drafting and notification procedures remain stable over multi-year periods unless major legislative overhauls occur.
